input:
This executive summary looks at a possible heat-recovery retrofit at a food plant and at whether the project should move forward at this stage. The plant currently uses 1827 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, which is a substantial part of the overall picture being considered here. According to the equipment vendor, the retrofit is projected to save 16% of that electricity use, which works out to a derived saving of 292 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost of the retrofit is $401k. Using an electricity price of $0.13 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $38k, and the derived simple payback period is 10.6 years.

It is important to note, however, that the saving figure is a vendor projection and has not been measured at this plant, and, furthermore, the refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, which introduces an additional element of uncertainty into the analysis. On the basis of these considerations, the recommendation is that a metered trial should be carried out on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken, so that the projected saving can be tested against an actual measurement on the plant's own load. The plant engineer owns the trial.
target:
Run a metered trial on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision on the heat-recovery retrofit; the plant engineer owns the trial. The recommendation rests on the size of the claim and the standing of the figure behind it. The food plant uses 1827 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, and the equipment vendor projects that the retrofit would save 16% of that use, a derived saving of 292 MWh per year at the vendor figure. Capital cost is $401k. At an electricity price of $0.13 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $38k and the derived simple payback is 10.6 years.

The trial is metered, so the saving it returns is a measured value on one line's refrigeration load over the trial period, set against the same line's present use.

The saving figure is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled. The payback stands or falls with the projected saving: a measured saving below the projection lengthens the payback in proportion, and the trial exists to replace the projection with a measurement on the plant's own load before capital is committed.
